answer: Each agent must lock a scarce deposit before its votes count, and the protocol slashes that deposit when a randomly selected claim fails a costly audit. An attacker can still create many identities, but cannot cheaply turn them into influence: every one needs separately locked capital, and false claims risk forfeiture. The capital is tied up during the voyage, while honest agents can reuse reputation across an orchard of tasks; the river of new identities therefore brings no free voting weight.
